title: Government Contract Brokering
uncertainty_note: Editorial sensitivity band, not a statistical interval. Confidence is a supplied classification; independent source review is required.

score_rationale.revenue_potential: Revenue Potential: 23/25. Simplified-acquisition (SAT) bid desks and disclosed subcontractor coordination earn repeatable agency spreads.
score_rationale.profit_margin_potential: Profit Margin Potential: 19/25. Simplified-acquisition (SAT) bid desks and disclosed subcontractor coordination earn repeatable agency spreads.
score_rationale.team_efficiency: Team Efficiency: 16/20. Simplified-acquisition (SAT) bid desks and disclosed subcontractor coordination earn repeatable agency spreads.
score_rationale.startup_accessibility: Startup Accessibility: 11/15. Simplified-acquisition (SAT) bid desks and disclosed subcontractor coordination earn repeatable agency spreads.
score_rationale.automation_potential: Automation Potential: 10/15. Simplified-acquisition (SAT) bid desks and disclosed subcontractor coordination earn repeatable agency spreads.

economics.owner_net_profit_potential: $18,000–$300,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment
economics.includes_contractors_note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.
economics.revenue_basis: Recognized service fees, not client asset value
economics.cost_basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.
economics.estimate_status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data

conservative.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

base_case.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

regulatory_notes: Review contingent-fee restrictions, procurement integrity and anti-kickback rules.
Pass-through restrictions and set-aside rules can prohibit proposed structures.

plays.name: Public-Record & API Intelligence
plays.mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.
inputs: Court & probate dockets
State controller ledgers
Public licensing & entity APIs
workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence
Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold
Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution

platform_risks.trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals
platform_risks.impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry
platform_risks.detection_metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta
platform_risks.fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues

plays.name: Industry Award & Verified Directory 'Ego-Bait' Badge Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Publish data-scored state and city rankings ('Top 15 Verified Specialists in [City]') and issue free embeddable 'Top Rated' winner badges to ranked firms—earning hundreds of free high-DR backlinks when firms post the badge on their own sites, while upselling $299–$799/mo Featured #1 Lead-Capture placements.
inputs: Public state licensing, inspection, & review dataset for 500+ firms per vertical
Transparent algorithmic scoring rubric + auto-generated SVG 'Verified Top 10%' embed badges
Self-serve $299–$799/mo Featured Placement & exclusive lead-routing checkout
workflow: Score all licensed operators in a high-ticket vertical using objective public records (years licensed, zero disciplinary actions, review velocity)
Notify top-scoring firms with their free embeddable HTML/SVG '2026 Top-Scored Provider' badge (driving natural dofollow backlinks back to your directory)
Convert 5–10% of shortlisted firms into $299–$799/mo Featured Top-Spot subscribers who receive priority inbound quote requests
metrics: Badge embed rate (% of notified firms linking back to directory)
Domain Rating (DR) growth and organic city-ranking velocity
Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) from Featured Profile subscriptions

platform_risks.failure_mode: FTC endorsement/ranking disclosure scrutiny or Google widget-link spam filtering
platform_risks.trigger: Manipulating objective scores solely for pay-to-play without 'Sponsored' labels or stuffing keyword-anchor links inside badge HTML
platform_risks.impact: Loss of editorial credibility or discounting of badge backlinks
platform_risks.detection_metric: Anchor-text naturalness ratio and clear visual separation of 'Sponsored Featured Partner' vs. algorithmic score
platform_risks.fallback: Keep the underlying algorithmic score 100% objective and immutable, clearly label paid top-spot placements as 'Sponsored / Featured', and use clean branded anchor text in badge embeds

plays.name: SAM.gov / Municipal RFP Scraping & Prime-Subcontractor Spread Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Scrape federal SAM.gov, state procurement portals, and municipal bid boards for low-bid-density service solicitations (janitorial, grounds, courier, translation, IT staffing), pairing compliant proposal automation with vetted local fulfillment subcontractors for a 15–30% management spread.
inputs: SAM.gov Contract Opportunities API & state/municipal e-procurement feeds
Historical FPDS award pricing benchmark database
Vetted local subcontractor network with FAR limitation-on-subcontracting compliance
workflow: Screen daily federal, state, and municipal RFPs/RFQs with <3 historical bidders and clear unit-price schedules
Benchmark winning historical unit rates via FPDS/FOIA award records and lock in binding back-to-back quotes from insured local operators
Submit compliant bid packages and manage billing, insurance, and QA reporting while retaining a 15–30% prime-management or authorized broker spread
metrics: Bid-to-award win rate (%) on low-competition solicitations

platform_risks.failure_mode: FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting) violation or illegal pass-through scheme
platform_risks.trigger: Bidding small-business set-aside contracts and subcontracting 100% of the work to non-similarly-situated entities without performing required prime share
platform_risks.impact: Contract termination for default, False Claims Act liability, or SAM.gov debarment
platform_risks.detection_metric: Subcontracted labor-cost percentage strictly within FAR 52.219-14 limits (<=50% for services unless partnering with similarly situated small businesses)
platform_risks.fallback: Bid unrestricted commercial/municipal contracts without set-aside caps, or team exclusively with 'similarly situated entities' under 13 CFR § 125.6

plays.name: Transferable Federal & State Tax Credit Brokerage & Syndication (IRA § 6418 / Film / Historic)
plays.mechanism: Scraping federal DOE/EPA interconnection queues, state film offices, and historic-preservation registries to originate transferable tax credits (IRC § 6418 Clean Energy Investment/Production Credits, Georgia/Louisiana Film Credits, State Historic Rehab & Brownfield Credits) from cash-strapped project developers at $0.82–$0.88 on the dollar and flipping them in simultaneous escrow closings to corporate and HNW taxpayers at $0.92–$0.96 on the dollar.
inputs: State film-office production certifications, National Park Service Part 2/3 Historic Preservation filings, and utility solar/biogas/storage interconnection queues
IRS Energy Credits Online pre-filing registration verification and tax-credit recapture insurance underwriting partners
Outbound network of CPA managing partners, corporate tax directors, and family-office CIOs with $1M–$50M+ in quarterly federal/state tax liabilities
workflow: Monitor public project registries to identify middle-market solar, RNG, battery storage, independent film, and historic-rehab developers holding $1M–$25M in newly generated transferable credits
Lock up exclusive purchase or placement options at $0.83–$0.89 per $1.00 of credit prior to quarterly corporate estimated tax deadlines (April 15, June 15, Sept 15, Dec 15)
Package the credits with a third-party CPA cost-segregation/eligibility opinion and tax-credit recapture insurance policy

Execute a simultaneous bilateral escrow closing with a corporate taxpayer at $0.92–$0.95 on the dollar—saving the buyer 5–8% guaranteed on their tax bill while capturing a 400–800 bps riskless spread ($40k–$80k per $1M block)
metrics: Face value of tax credits placed per quarter ($5M–$100M+)
Net retained principal/brokerage spread (400–800 bps) per closed tranche
Days in escrow from developer IRS registration number issuance to wire settlement

platform_risks.failure_mode: IRS § 6418 recapture event or state department-of-revenue basis challenge
platform_risks.trigger: Project developer inflating eligible cost basis or taking a clean-energy asset out of service during the 5-year recapture window
platform_risks.impact: Taxpayer recapture assessment plus penalties if uninsured
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% independent Big-4/national CPA cost-basis audit and mandatory A-rated tax-credit recapture insurance binder on every tranche
platform_risks.fallback: Never take unhedged balance-sheet inventory risk; close strictly via simultaneous back-to-back escrow funded by the buyer's wire and backed by non-cancelable tax-credit insurance

plays.name: White-Label MVNO & Federal/State Low-Income Telecom Subsidy Aggregation
plays.mechanism: Launching a white-label Mobile Virtual Network Operator (MVNO) or partnering as a master enrollment aggregator for Eligible Telecommunications Carriers (ETCs) to enroll hundreds of thousands of SNAP/Medicaid/SSI-eligible households into '100% Free Unlimited Talk/Text/Data' plans—arbitraging the spread between $2–$4/mo wholesale MVNO network COGS and $9.25–$44+/mo in combined Federal Lifeline, Tribal, and State (e.g., California LifeLine) monthly government reimbursements.
inputs: Wholesale MVNO Enabler (MVNE) agreement (T-Mobile/AT&T wholesale via Plum, Reach, Gigs) or master sub-agent contract with an ETC
National Verifier (USAC NLAD) API integration checking SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, and SSI eligibility in real time
Omnichannel street-team tablet canopy network and geotargeted digital co-registration funnels in high-subsidy zip codes
workflow: Target zip codes with high SNAP/Medicaid participation and stacked state-level telecom subsidies (e.g., California, Texas, Oklahoma, Tribal lands)
Verify applicant eligibility instantly against the USAC National Verifier / state administrator API and provision an instant eSIM or pre-activated pSIM
Pay enrollment agents or digital media channels a $15–$35 one-time acquisition bounty while collecting recurring monthly government reimbursements ($15–$44+/mo) plus upsold data top-ups
Automate 30-day usage heartbeats (outbound call/SMS check-ins) so enrolled lines satisfy mandatory USAC monthly active-usage rules
metrics: Active reimbursed subscriber base and monthly net ARPU ($12–$38/mo) vs. wholesale carrier COGS ($2.50–$4.50/mo)
Customer acquisition cost (CAC) payback period (target: <45 days)

platform_risks.failure_mode: USAC audit clawback for duplicate household enrollments or 30-day non-usage de-enrollment rules
platform_risks.trigger: Field agents enrolling ineligible subscribers or lines going 30 consecutive days without an outbound call, text, or data session
platform_risks.impact: Mandatory de-enrollment of inactive lines or USAC reimbursement recoupment
platform_risks.detection_metric: Rolling 20-day zero-usage cohort alerts and 100% NLAD/National Verifier API pre-check enforcement
platform_risks.fallback: Run automated Day-20 SMS/IVR engagement campaigns ('Reply YES to keep your free monthly service active') and strictly claw back field-agent commissions on any line failing 30-day usage

plays.name: GSA & Municipal Set-Aside Pass-Through Facility Ghost-Brokering
plays.mechanism: Match eligible facility-service primes with disclosed qualified subcontractors and earn documented coordination fees; opaque pass-throughs and false set-aside eligibility are excluded.
inputs: GSA and municipal facility solicitations
Prime eligibility and subcontracting-limit documentation
Licensed local vendor bids and capacity records
workflow: 1. Screen solicitations for service scope, eligibility, and permitted subcontracting
2. Verify the prime performs required work and disclose broker and subcontractor roles
3. Submit priced delivery plans with genuine vendor commitments and required certifications
4. Track service acceptance, payroll obligations, and authorized fee payments against contract terms

platform_risks.failure_mode: Set-aside eligibility protest or prohibited pass-through finding
platform_risks.trigger: Inaccurate certification or subcontracting beyond contract limits
platform_risks.impact: Termination, repayment demands, or debarment exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unverified certifications and subcontracted work share versus permitted limits
platform_risks.fallback: Withdraw noncompliant bids and operate as a disclosed subcontractor on unrestricted work

plays.name: IRC Section 179D Government & Nonprofit Energy-Deduction Allocation Brokering
plays.mechanism: Coordinate eligible government and tax-exempt building owners, qualifying designers, and independent energy certifiers to document Section 179D deduction allocations; compensation is for permitted services, not resale of a freely transferable deduction.
inputs: Public and nonprofit building project records and construction dates
Designer contracts and owner allocation authority
Independent energy certification and applicable tax-year eligibility rules
workflow: 1. Screen building projects for eligible ownership, construction timing, and current Section 179D availability
2. Verify qualifying designer work, energy certification, deduction limits, and applicable wage and apprenticeship requirements
3. Obtain authorized owner allocation letters and reconcile prior allocations to prevent duplicate deductions
4. Deliver the substantiated file to the designer's tax adviser and collect disclosed legally permitted coordination fees
metrics: Net coordination fees after certification and review costs

platform_risks.trigger: Ineligible project dates, unsupported designer status, deficient certification, or duplicate allocation
platform_risks.impact: Lost tax benefit, assessment exposure, and disputed service fees
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved eligibility and allocation exceptions per project
platform_risks.fallback: Pause allocation, obtain independent tax review, and offer fixed-fee documentation support only for eligible projects
